newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds outperform, ValuJet jumps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds outperform, ValuJet jumps.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds outperformed U.S. Treasuries in the intermediates sector while junk-rated ValuJet notes jumped on news the low-cost carrier's fleet could return to the skies, experts said.
"It seems like technically it's a tremendous market," said Dennis Adler, corporate bond strategist at Salomon Brothers Inc, regarding the investment-grade market.
"People can't find enough paper and investors need to put cash to work and are buying whatever they can find."
Adler added street inventory was being depleted and new issue volume has been disappointing over the past few months.
Yield spreads in the banking and finance sector and Korean, Quebec and Italian Yankees were quoted one to two basis points tighter in the middle maturities.
High-yields were also well bid on the day with prices up 1/8 to 1/4 of a point overall, dealers said.
ValuJet Inc debt gained more than three points after the U.S. Department of Transportation gave permission for the airline's planes to fly, dealers said.
Roughly half an hour after the much-anticipated announcement, price talk on ValuJet's $150 million 10.25 percent notes due 2001 had gained to a 90 bid, 91 offer.
While quotes were bid higher, few dealers said they had seen the completion of actual trades at these new levels.

The price of ValuJet debt slid 20 points to an 80 bid following news its Flight 592 crashed in the Florida Everglades on May 11. Ensuing negative press and the June 17 grounding of the fleet after a DOT safety inspection caused the notes to bottom out at a mid-60's bid in June.

Terex Corp debt was hammered almost three points lower to a 103 bid from a 105-3/4 bid at Wednesday's close on news its recently signed agreement for the sale of its Clark Material Handling Co to Clark Acquisition Corp had been terminated.
Iron Mountain Inc's $165 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced at par on Thursday to yield 10.125 percent, were bid at 102-1/2 out of the gate.

Telecom paper was up 1/4 to 1/2 point in general, according to one sector trader. Sprint Spectrum zero coupon bonds traded up 3/4 point to 58-1/2 compared with a 57-3/4 bid late Wednesday. Sprint Spectrum's 11 percent debt due 2006 was also higher at 103 bid, 103-1/2 offer.
Telecom issues priced last week, including debt from Gray Communications and Sygnet Wireless, were also active.
Gray's $150 million 10.625 percent notes were ended at a 102-1/2 bid and Sygnet's 11.50 percent notes closed at 103.

High-grade issuance featured $240 million 30-year Baa3/BBB rated bonds from News America Holdings Inc, priced at par to yield 7.43 percent or 78 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note. The bonds have a put in the tenth year.
Deal size was upped by $40 million due to strong demand, lead underwriter Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said. Dealers said the paper was relatively cheap for BBB-rated debt.
Tupperware Finance B.V. set $100 million in Baa2/BBB-plus rated 10-year notes at 99.838 to yield 7.273 percent or 62 basis points over the underlying Treasury.
Regarding issues still at bat for this week, Ford Motor Co is expected to issue $500 million in 12-year notes on Friday via Lehman Brothers, syndicate sources said Thursday.
Price talk on the A1/A-plus non-callable notes is 70 basis points. This incoming supply kept secondary spreads unchanged in the industrials sector on Thursday, dealers said.
Also, Boyd gaming is looking to price $200 million in seven-year senior notes via Salomon. Price talk ranges from 250 to 275 basis points.
-- Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677
